note: Scores 0-1000 are the author's judgement of expected learner value, not measured outcomes. improvedScore equals score when no improvement was specced. riskAxis: higher is worse.

concepts.name: Fixed two-page template per letter
concepts.what: Every letter gets the same pair of pages (story/picture page, then a write page), so the learner always knows what comes next.

concepts.name: Numbered stroke-order arrows on the model glyph
concepts.what: The modern-script model carries small numbers and arrows showing stroke order and direction (visible on the pages I rasterised; I did not check all 22).

concepts.name: Single heavy model glyph at the start of an RTL practice line, then blank ruled lines
concepts.what: One grey model sits at the right edge (the reading start) and the rest of the page is empty lines; no fading, no checking.

concepts.name: Picture hook per letter (object plus short story)
concepts.what: Each letter is tied to a drawn object and a two-sentence story, and a colouring task to fix the image. The hook is the book's main memory device.

spec.screen: Per-letter card showing a simple original image that echoes the print glyph's shape, a one-line cue, and the sound anchor word; a toggle swaps between two cues.
spec.data: Data: hooks[] per letter {cue, imageId, kind: shape or sound}, authored for ALEF, not taken from the book. Optional history line kept in a separate "origin" field and labelled as background.
spec.interaction: Learner picks the hook that works for them; a recall test later shows only the hook image and asks for the letter; hook usage informs which hooks stay.
spec.test: Unit: every letter has at least one hook, imageId resolves to an asset or is flagged pending, no hook text contradicts the letter's recorded sound; recall quiz returns the right answer for each hook.

concepts.notes: The specific objects and stories are the book's own expression and carry its theology; only the general technique (picture hook plus recall) is reused.

concepts.name: Three-script ancestry strip (pictograph, paleo, modern) beside each letter
concepts.what: Shows an old picture-form, an older script form and the modern form side by side so shape descent is visible.
concepts.notes: Interesting history, little reading payoff. The book presents each early form and each letter-meaning as settled fact; I did not verify those claims.

concepts.name: Three keyword "meanings" listed per letter
concepts.what: Each letter lists three English words (an object plus abstract ideas) as its meaning.
concepts.notes: Weak for both goals and the abstract meanings are unverified folklore; reject as learning content. The picture-hook technique (bk-bpa-04) is the only part worth keeping.

concepts.name: One-page alphabet chart with three script columns
concepts.what: A single reference table listing every letter, used as a lookup.

concepts.name: "Did you know" orientation box (right to left, count of letters, name plus sound)
concepts.what: Three facts up front before any letter.

concepts.name: Colouring task as retention device
concepts.what: Colour the picture to anchor the hook. Good for young children; adult value is low.

concepts.name: Alphabetical-only sequence, one letter at a time, no review
concepts.what: Alef to Tav in order with no cumulative review, no look-alike contrast and no sounds task.
concepts.notes: This is a weakness record, not an idea to adopt. See the gap concepts below.

concepts.name: Circle-the-target scan on running text (gap filler; not in the book)
concepts.what: The book never has the learner find a letter inside text. Cancellation-style scanning (find every instance of a target letter, ignoring look-alikes) trains the actual reading skill.

spec.screen: New drill screen "Spot It" reachable from a letter lesson and from the review queue. Shows 3 to 5 lines of pointed Hebrew, right to left, in the learner's chosen script; a target letter chip sits at the top right.
spec.data: Pure builder over the corpus registry and the confusables list: for target T pick lines containing T and plant its confusable partners (for example bet/kaf, dalet/resh) as decoys. Output {lineIds, targetId, hitIndices, decoyIndices}. Difficulty ladder: single letters, then words, then a verse line. Results feed the existing progress store as per-letter and per-confusable-pair accuracy.
spec.interaction: Tap or stylus-circle every instance of the target; decoys that are tapped count against the confusable pair and re-queue that pair in the SRS; a timer is optional and off by default; finishing shows hits, misses and which decoy fooled the learner.
spec.test: Unit: builder returns hit indices equal to the true count of T in the line, never marks a decoy as a hit, and is deterministic with a seed. Data guard: only lines whose letters are all taught by that lesson. UI: mount/unmount leaves no listeners.

concepts.printable: Printable page kind "scan": one target letter in a box at the top right, 6 ruled lines of unpointed then pointed text, instruction "circle every one"; answer key page lists the count per line. Spec only; reuse the buildModel/buildHtml page-kind convention in tools/letters/workbook.mjs.

concepts.name: Sound-to-letter matching with a keyword per sound (gap filler)
concepts.what: The book teaches shape and writing but never ties shape to sound on the page. Matching glyph to a sound cue is the missing link.

spec.screen: Two-column matcher: left column plays an audio clip (no transliteration), right column shows 4 candidate glyphs including one look-alike; sits after the tap-to-hear atlas.
spec.data: Per-letter keyword anchor (an everyday word whose first sound is the letter's sound) stored in letters.json as proposed field soundAnchor, one per tradition where sounds differ; reuses audio manifest ids kind=letter.
spec.interaction: Hear, pick the glyph, get immediate audio plus the anchor word on a miss; misses of look-alikes are logged into the confusables SRS queue.
spec.test: Unit: distractor builder never includes the target twice and always contains one confusable partner when one exists; accuracy logging writes to the progress store; every referenced audio id exists in the manifest.

concepts.printable: Printable "match the sound" page needs audio so is not good on paper; use a keyword-anchor page instead (draw a line from glyph to the picture word). Spec only.

concepts.name: Tap a big letter, instantly hear it (grid of all tiles)
concepts.what: One screen of tiles; tapping one opens a single letter and plays audio. Zero setup, zero reading needed.

concepts.name: Each form-plus-sound pair is its own tile (32 entries, repeated names for variants and finals)
concepts.what: The grid lists repeated names (for example three Kaf tiles, two Mem, two Nun, three Pe, two Shin), which I read as dagesh and final variants. The page does not label which is which, so this is my inference.

spec.screen: Atlas screen: a right-to-left grid of all 27 letters plus the dagesh and shin-dot variants as separately labelled tiles, each tile showing glyph, its form state (plain, dagesh, final) and a small sound label for the active tradition.
spec.data: Derived, not hand-typed: built from letters.json and niqqud.json variant rules, 31 form-sound units to match the printable workbook's 31 rows. Each tile links audio id kind=letter plus a sibling list (bet to vet, kaf to khaf, finals to their regular forms).
spec.interaction: Tap a tile: audio plays in the chosen voice and tradition, the sibling tiles pulse; long-press shows stroke order. A "sound merges here" badge appears on pairs that sound identical in the chosen tradition (for example Israeli chet and khaf).
spec.test: Unit: tile count equals 31; every tile has an audio id that resolves in the manifest or falls back to Web Speech; tiles are ordered right to left; sibling links are symmetric; merge badges match the pronunciation data for each tradition.

concepts.name: One tradition stated plainly above the grid
concepts.what: A note says pronunciation is Sephardic Israeli. Honest, but there is no way to change it.
concepts.notes: ALEF already has a congregation setting; keep the up-front statement, add per-tradition playback.

concepts.name: Letters laid out left to right with an apology note
concepts.what: The page admits the grid contradicts reading direction. For a siddur-reading goal this teaches the wrong spatial habit.
concepts.notes: Weakness record. ALEF shows tiles right to left everywhere.

concepts.name: Read first, write later as separate courses
concepts.what: The page points to separate reading and writing crash courses, with writing described as reinforcing earlier reading. Their claim of 250,000 learners is the organisation's own figure, which I did not verify.

concepts.name: Built-in accessibility toolbar (contrast, text size, readable font, reduced motion)
concepts.what: A widget adjusts contrast, size and animation.

concepts.name: Weakness: audio only; no quiz, no stroke order, no memory hook stated on the page
concepts.what: The page offers listening and nothing to test recall. I could only see the static HTML, so interactions inside the lightbox are unseen.

concepts.name: Letters taught in small alphabetical groups with a midterm
concepts.what: Course sections run Alef-Dalet up to Resh-Tav with a midterm in the middle (from the public outline; group sizes beyond the first and last were not shown).

spec.screen: Lesson plan view groups letters by look-alike sets separated across lessons (so bet and kaf are not introduced together), with a checkpoint after each third of the alphabet.
spec.data: Grouping rule applied over confusables.json when generating lessons; checkpoint is a mixed quiz drawing from everything taught so far.
spec.interaction: Checkpoint results move items between SRS stages; failure sends the learner to the relevant Spot It or matching drill.
spec.test: Unit: no lesson contains two letters flagged confusable unless the lesson is a contrast lesson; each checkpoint draws only taught letters.

concepts.name: Hebrew keyboard setup in lecture one
concepts.what: Typing is introduced up front so the learner can type letters and search.

concepts.name: Dedicated "recognise handwriting" block after print letters
concepts.what: A separate section on handwritten letter forms, run in letter groups (Alef-Hey through Pey-Tav).

spec.screen: Drill screen "Read the handwriting" shown after the print letters are known. Each card shows one letter or a short word in ktav yad, with a print-script reveal on tap.
spec.data: Uses the cursive glyph data already in letters.json (cursive strokes derived from an OFL font) plus a stylus-sample variation layer: random slant, stroke weight and joining jitter generated client-side. Optional extension: learner's own tracing from the trace view saved as a personal sample.
spec.interaction: Forced-choice from 4 print candidates; the confusable cursive pairs are weighted up (cursive shapes that collide); after a miss the stroke-order animation of the cursive form plays once. Unlocks after 12 letters are mature in SRS.
spec.test: Unit: jitter keeps the glyph inside its box and is deterministic with a seed; candidate set always includes the true letter once; unlock gate respects the SRS maturity threshold; every card passes the shape check in src/letters/shapecheck.js.

concepts.printable: Printable page kind "handwriting": a row of 8 jittered cursive samples with print-letter boxes to fill in. Spec only.

concepts.name: Letters only, no vowel signs
concepts.what: The course scope is letter names and pronunciation without niqqud; the public description says so.
concepts.notes: Weakness for ALEF goals: a learner cannot read a single word yet. Short scope is a strength for a free funnel course only.

concepts.name: Overview PDF cheat sheet
concepts.what: A downloadable one-pager of the alphabet.

concepts.name: Video lecture format (about 55 minutes total)
concepts.what: Passive watching; no stroke or recall mechanism is visible in the outline.

concepts.name: "You already know some Hebrew" opener (cognates and loanwords as the first words)
concepts.what: The listing shows Chapter 1 is framed around words an English speaker already knows. Reuse the idea only: first reading words are ones the learner can already understand.
concepts.improvedName: Words you can already read (loanword on-ramp)

spec.screen: Lesson card "You can already read this": after the first 8 to 10 letters the learner decodes Israeli loanwords written in Hebrew, one at a time, with the English meaning hidden until they attempt it.
spec.data: New list data/vocab loanwords (proposed): {he pointed, he plain, gloss, source language, lettersUsed[], tradition notes}. Selection rule: every letter in the word already taught, no vowel signs needed beyond what the lesson has shown. Needs native-speaker review before shipping and attribution is not required because the words are common vocabulary, but I have not checked any specific candidate list.
spec.interaction: See word, tap letters to hear syllables, type or pick the English meaning, then hear the word in both voices. The learner can mark "I knew this" for a quick pass.
spec.test: Unit: for each word, lettersUsed is a subset of the lesson's taught letters, pointed text passes the U+0590-05FF check, and no word appears before its letters are taught. Review flag status must be set to needs-native-review.

concepts.name: Pre-teaching sounds English speakers lack (gutturals and similar)
concepts.what: The publisher description says the book prepares readers for unfamiliar sounds. Treated here as a dedicated sound-gap step instead of folding these letters in with easy ones.

spec.screen: A short lab screen reached after the first consonants: three pairs of sounds English readers blur, each as a listen-and-pick minimal-pair drill (chet versus khaf, kaf versus qof, tet versus tav). The set shown depends on the chosen tradition because merges differ.
spec.data: Pair table keyed by tradition in data/pronunciation (proposed pairs.json): {a, b, traditions where they are distinct, audio ids}. Pairs that are merged in a tradition are shown as "same sound here" rather than drilled.
spec.interaction: Hear one clip, tap the letter; a mouth-position tip card appears on a miss; recording self-compare is out of scope until the audio lane supports it.
spec.test: Unit: every pair references real letter ids and audio ids; merged pairs are never drilled in the tradition where they merge; no pair data contradicts the pronunciation data files. Human check: a native speaker confirms which pairs are distinct per tradition.

concepts.name: Contrast framing: where Hebrew resembles English and where it differs
concepts.what: Explanations are anchored in what the English reader will get wrong or right by instinct.
concepts.improvedName: Interference hints triggered by the learner's own error

spec.screen: Inline hint panel under a wrong answer: one sentence saying what an English reader tends to expect and what Hebrew does instead (reading direction, missing short vowels, silent letters).
spec.data: Hint library keyed by error type: {errorKind, hint, appliesTo tradition}; error kinds come from the drill results already logged (confusable pair, wrong vowel, direction slip).
spec.interaction: Show the hint only after a miss, once per error kind per session, with a "got it" button that suppresses it for that kind next time; repeated misses escalate to a worked example.
spec.test: Unit: every errorKind made by the drills has a hint; hints are under 140 characters; suppression state persists in the store; a hint never appears on a correct answer.

concepts.name: Parts ordered: basics, everyday action, travel, deeper life, sacred Hebrew last
concepts.what: A functional Hebrew path with the sacred register as its own late part, shown by the table of contents.
concepts.notes: ALEF runs these as two parallel tracks (read and israel) from day one, which suits the two stated goals better.

concepts.name: Exercises with an answer key appendix
concepts.what: The table of contents ends with an answer key, which implies printed exercises that the learner can self-mark.

concepts.name: Verb tables and mini-dictionary appendices
concepts.what: Reference tables for lookup.

concepts.name: Online audio of native speakers in conversation
concepts.what: The description says audio of native speakers in dialogue accompanies the book.

concepts.name: Part of Tens: ten-item quick-win lists
concepts.what: A closing section of short top-ten lists (content not shown in the listing).
